title: Mole Calculations

problems_fixed.what: Problem was non-physical: 5.6 g / 0.25 mol gives Mr 22.4, which matches no gas and contradicts the 'diatomic element, Ar 14' clue (would need Mr 28). Changed mass 5.6 g -> 7.0 g so Mr = 7.0/0.25 = 28 = N2 (nitrogen), making the display, answer and 'name the gas' clue self-consistent.

misconceptions_note: All misconceptions previously had no 'expect' key (validator would reject). Added determinate 'expect' values derived by committing each error (forgot-ratio, inverse, unit x1000, stopping at Mr); set expect:null where the error has no single value (generic wrong_Mr / wrong_count / 1:1-ratio cases). All expects verified outside the accept window and none equal the correct answer.
guided_added: tier_guides (bronze/silver/gold), guided.opener (weighing coins to count them = n = m/Mr), guided.teach walks (CH4 moles / 2Mg+O2 1:1 ratio / CH4 combustion 1:2 ratio), guided_steps on 19 of 20 problems, per-problem hints on all 20, tier descriptions.

guided_skips.reason: Single multiplication by the Avogadro constant giving ~3x10^23; cannot be entered box-by-box at the engine's +-0.005 tolerance.

figures_note: Pure chemistry formula lesson (moles, Mr, reacting masses, concentration). No circuit or graph problems, so no SVG/chart figures per the diagram-pass 'no decoration on pure-formula problems' rule.
board_neutral_note: OCR-B row (single id). No board named; no equation-sheet claims. Chemistry has no formula sheet, so equations are simply taught.

opener_concept: Counting atoms by weighing, framed as counting coins in a bag by weighing (total mass / mass of one = count).
